correctness.rationale: The crown adjacency off-diagonal block is 11*−I. For n≥3 its adjacency has distinct levels ±(n−1), ±1. Nonempty T rules out both principal vectors; at either remaining level the absorber equations delete exactly the touched indices from a zero-sum coordinate vector. Their direct sum is the stated dark space, with one zero-sum summand per shore. It reduces the loss generator; on the complement any imaginary-axis eigenvector would have zero dissipation and thus be an adjacency eigenvector vanishing at T, a contradiction. Strictly negative real parts imply decay there even with Jordan blocks. The complementary orthogonal projector gives the pure/mixed and sitewise laws, including all-marked and one-unmarked cases. Complete capture is equivalent to at least n−1 distinct touched indices, not arbitrary placements of n−1 vertices; minimal successful placements number n·2^(n−1). Adding the second member of an already touched pair changes no eventual capture probability; this is the meaning of the redundancy example.
residual_risks: The finite projection check does not test arbitrary rates or finite-time decay. Those are handled only to the extent of the analytic eventual-capture argument; no rate bound is claimed.

value.rationale: The crown family is a standard graph with large degenerate eigenspaces. The full capture effect for every absorber placement distinguishes strategies with the same cardinality, gives efficiency even at a site not itself absorbing, and yields exact minimal design counts independently of positive rate heterogeneity. These are useful inputs for coherent transport calculations; the known spectrum and a generic rank test are not themselves the placement law.
residual_risks: No claim about capture times, rate optimization, or nonuniform hopping.
